notes:
I couldn't write the Psalm 40 notes this time. The research tool stopped working before I could read any pages, so I don't have a single page I can cite.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. If I wrote notes now, they would come from my own memory, not your approved sites, so I've left them out rather than invent sources.

When you run this again, these are the pages I planned to read first:

- **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-40/; biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/40.htm (also the Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages, which use the same address with "gill" or "pulpit" in place of "ellicott"); preceptaustin.org's Psalm 40 commentary.
- **Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Psalm 40:** on spurgeon.org or ccel.org.
- **Calvin's commentary on Psalm 40:** on ccel.org.
- **Wesley's notes on Psalms:** on wesley.nnu.edu.
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes, especially on vv. 6–8 ("my ears You have opened") and on how the end of the psalm, vv. 13–17, also appears as Psalm 70.
  - Augustine's sermon on Psalm 40 on newadvent.org. His numbering is one lower, so it's listed as Psalm 39.
  - Catholic and Orthodox pages on catholic.com and oca.org.

Verses 6–8 will probably need the most work. They are where Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes the Greek version ("a body You prepared for me"), and where readers most often disagree about whether the psalm speaks about Christ.
